items.title: A forward-Euler Fisher–KPP reaction step preserves its interval under a sharp simple bound

references.title: Willem Hundsdorfer, Numerical Solution of Advection-Diffusion-Reaction Equations, lecture notes for Ph.D. course, 1996
references.locator: §6, printed pp. 39–40: forward-Euler positivity bounds for reaction updates; the scalar interval calculation is verified here.

items.statement: Let $r>0$ and use the scalar Fisher–KPP reaction $F(u)=ru(1-u)$ on $R=[0,1]$, followed by exact no-flux TPFA diffusion with any diffusivity $d\ge0$. For a nonnegative step $\tau$, the forward-Euler reaction map preserves $[0,1]$ for every starting value $u\in[0,1]$ exactly when $0\le\tau r\le1$; after that step, exact no-flux TPFA diffusion also preserves the interval. For $\tau>0$, on any finite grid with positive cell weights, the reaction strictly increases the discrete mass if at least one cell value lies in $(0,1)$ and leaves it unchanged if every cell value is a reaction equilibrium $0$ or $1$. At $\tau=0$ the reaction map is the identity. This example makes no mass-conservation claim.
